problem: Six fact-consuming responses across two studies failed to use the supplied conditional facts. Two root-only controls correctly abstained; all eight study responses omitted the requested runtime caveat.
hypothesis: A small bilingual template attached to a fresh guarded closed-source observation can answer this one admitted question without model inference, preserving exact entry identity, integer and runtime uncertainty.
input: Trusted operator-created ClosedDependencyObserver, explicit stable question ID and requested module/symbol; never accept a returned JSON fact packet as authority.
output: Paired EN/PT question and answer in memory, full source observation, stable question kind/ID, text hash, no publication or training approval.
boundaries: Fresh source/registry/code checks come from the guarded observer.
Only the admitted static integer-return question is supported.
Inconclusive observation yields no answer pair and never recommends removing documentation.
No file writes, model calls, default Ruby route, arbitrary prose or automatic FAQ installation.
A pair text hash detects wording changes, not source identity or owner permission.
controls: Formatting-only helper change alters evidence but preserves pair bytes
Stale/missing source or configuration drift refuses
JSON packet cannot impersonate an observer
Both languages retain identifiers, integer and runtime-binding caveat
acceptance: Every admitted development source gives the exact conditional integer in both languages; unsupported cases produce no answer.0modelcalls.
split: Same exposed owned synthetic family, not independent holdout.
